newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU helps British, Dutch, Danish regions in decline.
newsitem.headline: EU helps British, Dutch, Danish regions in decline.

text.p: The European Commission agreed on Wednesday to unblock over 2.8 billion European currency units ($3.2 billion) to help regions in industrial decline in Britain, the Netherlands, Denmark and Belgium.
The bulk of the EU money -- 2.5 billon ecus -- will be spent in a dozen British regions ranging from Western Scotland to the West Midlands and East London, the Commission said in a statement.

It said the EU aid will be matched by British public funds of about 2.8 billion ecus while 819 million ecus will come from the private sector. The development programmes approved by the Commission are expected to create more than 150,000 jobs.

The northern Dutch provinces of Groningen and Drenthe, the South-East Brabant region in the south of the country and the Arnhem-Nijmegen area in the Rhine basin on the German border will receive a total 297.16 million ecus from the EU coffers.
The Dutch government will contribute 456 million ecus towards the financing of projects designed to create 15,700 jobs.

The Commission also gave its support to the industrial reconstruction of Denmark's southern island of Lolland by approving 13.8 million ecus towards projects in the services sector, in particular tourism.
Finally, it cleared 1.01 million ecus for the Belgian town of Aubange, on the border with Luxembourg.
